purpose: Review public W3C discovery, technical-standard reading, accessibility guidance and contact routes across varied templates; distinguish W3C sustainability advocacy from evidence about operating www.w3.org.

pages.task: Discover W3C standards, missions and public resources.
pages.rationale: Public institutional homepage and navigation entry point.

pages.task: Find a technical report by title or shortname using the public catalogue.
pages.rationale: Interactive searchable/filterable catalogue; substantively different from reading pages.

pages.rationale: Long technical-report template, references and versioning.

pages.task: Find introductory accessibility resources for a new practitioner.
pages.rationale: WAI overview template and audience-oriented resource discovery.

pages.task: Learn how to provide appropriate text alternatives for different image purposes.
pages.rationale: Instructional tutorial with examples and distinct WAI navigation.

pages.task: Understand W3C sustainability work and follow its published guideline resources.

pages.task: Find the appropriate public contact route without sending a message.
pages.rationale: Practical organizational task distinct from standards reading.

journeys.task: Find and open WCAG 2.2 from the homepage through the searchable standards catalogue.

contextScopes.access-barriers: Anonymous English desktop readers with JavaScript enabled, a pointer and ordinary text input at 1365x900: start at https://www.w3.org/, follow standards to the public technical-report catalogue, filter for WCAG and open the full WCAG 2.2 report. Completion requires its exact URL and visible full report title, with no account or personal-data submission. Keyboard-only, mobile, impaired-network and geographic access are not represented.
contextScopes.content-lifecycle: Public English WCAG 2.2 technical-report collection, from the first 2020 working draft through the December 2024 Recommendation and its currently published history as captured on 2026-11-06: review stated maintenance/review arrangements, an applied publication/update decision and discoverable historical reports. The broader WAI collection and organization-wide CMS practices are excluded; continuing reference value of historical standards is retained.
contextScopes.sustainability-goals: Operation and delivery of the public www.w3.org web service as described by its sustainability mission page at the 2026-11-06 capture. Assess whether published direction, metrics, service boundary and dated comparable baseline/progress refer to this service. W3C advocacy for the wider web and development of WSG are context, not evidence of this service achieving operational targets.

contextEvidence.scope: Published W3C sustainability mission and work descriptions, captured 2026-11-06.
contextEvidence.limitations: Attributed publisher self-report and rendered public-document capture; no internal or independent operational verification. Excerpt limits, publication dates and source URLs are recorded in the capture.

assumptions: Desktop first-load headline; narrow viewport and preferences are supplementary
No form submission or account change unless explicitly scoped
Setup browsing verifies reachability and journey mechanics only; it provides no transfer, energy or conformance measurement.
No cookie controls observed on sampled pages in fresh anonymous Chromium context; explicit no_banner branches selected.
Energy experiment will be run later, sequentially with competing local work paused; planned homepage sample has three repetitions.
Public self-reporting is attributed; current sustainability performance is not inferred from brand, mission or historical studies.
ownerPriorities: Public-only fresh audit across varied site types; evidence-backed findings and explicit unknowns.
scopeOmissions: Member-only, account, invited-expert and authenticated areas; no form submission or email sending.
Other languages, mobile and keyboard-only journeys, comprehensive standards coverage, events, membership and external subdomains.
Data-minimization omitted: selected tasks read public information and filter a catalogue, without collecting personal data.
Audience-needs and inclusive-testing omitted: WAI guidance about inclusive practice does not document representative testing of a selected www.w3.org interface decision.

Governance-practice, impact-business-model and service-necessity omitted: no bounded operational commitment or creation/funding decision selected; a mission statement alone cannot establish implementation.
Service-end-of-life omitted: no selected retirement/continuity task.
unresolvedEvidenceRequests: For content-lifecycle: a public review/maintenance schedule and a reasoned WCAG 2.2 update example; visible publication history alone may not establish review cadence.
For sustainability-goals: any dated operational metric, comparable baseline and progress for www.w3.org itself; WSG publishing activity alone does not meet this boundary.
